rashi:a1.1: Or perhaps… If you say at the first meal…: For if you say [it is fed] at every meal, there is no further question, since we certainly do not care whether it is before eating or after eating: at the second meal it is after [the first] eating, and still we feed it. But if you say that we give it only at the first meal of each day, we have a question.
rashi:a1.2: Before eating it certainly helps it like a medicine: in the manner of a medicine, for every person drinks a medicine for healing before eating.
rashi:a1.3: After eating, what? Does it count as an examination this way or not?
rashi:a1.4: This is the reading: Before drinking it certainly helps it like barley: for it is the way of an animal to eat barley before drinking.
rashi:a2.1: Untied, it certainly helps it: for it feels at ease.
rashi:a2.2: With another: it is at ease in company, and the eating helps it.
rashi:a3.1: In the field: it is at ease in the open air.
rashi:a3.2: A garden adjacent to the city: is it like a field or not?
rashi:a4.1: That they be divided into thirds: into three parts. If he sees it today, he examines it from now until day twenty-six and a half, and again after another twenty-six and a half, and again on day twenty-seven [of the last third], so that they make eighty. For at these three intervals that blemish, [if it is a temporary one,] tends to pass and not be seen, and then it is a passing blemish.
tosafot:a4.1: In brief: “Divided into thirds” means at the beginning of the eighty days, at the end and in the middle. Tosafot reads Megilla 19a the same way, where a scroll sewn with three threads of sinew is fit “provided they are divided into thirds”: at the top of the sheet, in its middle and at its bottom; there Rashi explained that the distance from the top of the sheet to the stitch should be like that from stitch to stitch, above and below. In Makkot 9b, about the cities of refuge, “divided into thirds” certainly means equal distances: from the south to Hebron as from Hebron to Shechem, from Hebron to Shechem as from Shechem to Kedesh, and from Shechem to Kedesh as from Kedesh to the north; not at the beginning, end and middle of the Land of Israel. Here Rashi explained “three parts”: if he sees it today he examines it on day twenty-six and a half, and again, until day eighty; he seems to have explained this along the lines of Makkot. But it is not fully like Makkot either, for then he should have explained that one examines at the end of twenty, of forty and of sixty, so that twenty of the eighty days remain after the last examination, just as there are twenty before the first. Tosafot holds it cannot be explained so at all, but as first explained, as is implied in Yevamot 80a about a congenital eunuch: “anyone who has not seen an hour of fitness”; the Gemara asks, let us worry that he became healthy in between, and answers that since his beginning and end are afflicted we do not worry. This implies that three times means its beginning, its end and its middle. And it seems that the villages “divided into thirds” of Eruvin 57a are like neither this nor Makkot. rashi:a6.1: To misuse its redemption: the question is not about a firstborn, to which redemption does not apply, but about other consecrated animals whose eyes were dripping. He immediately set aside their redemption and said, “They are hereby deconsecrated onto these coins,” and afterward they examined it, and before its three-month examination period ended, someone benefited from the redemption money.
rashi:a6.2: If you say it is a retroactive blemish: it turns out that its deconsecration was a [valid] deconsecration and its redemption money is sacred, and one brings an offering for misuse.
rashi:a7.1: Shmuel read about him: this verse, “the lame take the prey,” which is something the mind cannot bear, that the lame should take spoils. That is to say: you are not sharp, and yet you asked such a question that I do not know the answer.
rashi:a9.1: Gemara. On the outside: where the hole is seen, that is, the outer walls of the nose were pierced.
rashi:a9.2: On the inside: where the partition dividing the nose was pierced.
rashi:a9.3: It is not a blemish: since it is in a concealed place.
rashi:a9.4: Tura bara deshiftei: the outer row of the lip, that is, the edge of the lip and not its breadth.
rashi:a10.1: Mishna. The mat’imot [double teeth]: large teeth, (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), where one looks like two.
rashi:a10.2: And not even the double teeth: so that if the gums opposite them were extracted, it is not a blemish.
rashi:a11.1: Gemara. Which is the double tooth: all of it is explained below.
rashi:a11.2: And the double tooth itself is like the inward part: and one does not slaughter on its account.
rashi:a11.3: The outer ones: those in the middle of the mouth.
rashi:a11.4: One does not pay attention: for it is not even disqualified from the altar.
rashi:a12.1: What is it saying: in that it says, “Which is the double tooth? From the double tooth and inward.”
rashi:a13.1: This is what it is saying: Which is the inner [gum]? The one about which we say in the mishna: if they were extracted it is a blemish; if damaged or scratched it is not a blemish.
rashi:a14.1: But it is disqualified: from upon the altar, and he waits until it develops another blemish and slaughters it.
rashi:a15.1: “Lameness or blindness” is written: implying exposed, yes; concealed, no.
rashi:a16.1: To be slaughtered: a firstborn, for a lack on the inside.
rashi:a16.2: Or to be redeemed: [other] consecrated animals, I have no question, since it does not count as a blemish to that extent.
rashi:a17.1: To be accepted: by the altar.
rashi:a18.1: And the two kidneys: written [in the verses] about offerings.
rashi:a18.2: He shall take it away: implying one kidney: he shall take it away and burn it.
rashi:a19.1: There is no creature with one: no creature is created with one kidney, and this one that has only one has become lacking.
rashi:a19.2: This one: the baraita that disqualifies is where it was created with two and they became lacking, for we see that its place is noticeable; and that baraita that declares it fit is, for example, where it was created with one, so there is no lack.
rashi:a22.1: One Sage, who disqualifies, holds that there is no creature with one: and this one is certainly lacking. My teacher was uncertain why [the Gemara] does not also challenge him [here]: “it teaches it like three.” But to me it is no difficulty at all. When we thought that everyone agrees there is a creature with one, we challenged: since there is a creature with one, and he taught it together with three, then one created with one is certainly unfit too, and we would not know why it is unfit, since it is not an exposed blemish and there is no lack on the inside. Because of this refutation they established it according to the one who holds there is no creature with one, and this one has become lacking; and necessarily it is not like three, since there is no creature with one. And if you say, let us establish it according to the one who holds there is a creature with one: if so, why is it unfit?
rashi:a23.1: It lacked before slaughter: it is disqualified.
gershom:a1.1: It helps like a medicine: for it is the way of every medicine and every drink to help more before eating than after eating.
gershom:a2.1: It helps it like barley: for barley is better for an animal to eat before drinking than after drinking.
gershom:a3.1: After drinking, what? Does this moist and dry [fodder] help it after drinking or not?
gershom:a4.1: Tied or untied: that is, when he feeds it moist and dry, must he untie the firstborn, since it eats more happily when it is untied?
gershom:a5.1: A garden adjacent to the city: and he feeds it there; does the air of the garden help it like the air of the field?
gershom:a6.1: Provided that they are divided into thirds: that is, at the end of twenty-seven, twenty-seven and twenty-seven [days].
gershom:a7.1: It ate: moist and dry for three months and was not healed: is it a blemish retroactively, from the time it began to have it?
gershom:a8.1: To misuse its redemption: if he redeemed it within the period, before the three months were complete.
gershom:a9.1: If you say it is a retroactive blemish: it is redeemed, and one who benefits from the redemption money has misused.
gershom:a10.1: And if you say it is a blemish from here on and not before, the redemption does not take hold, for it is still unblemished, and one who benefits from the redemption money has not misused.
gershom:a11.1: Shmuel read about him: about Rav Pineḥas. [Rabbeinu Gershom calls him Rav Pineḥas; the daf has Pineḥas.]
gershom:a12.1: The lame take the prey: that is, although his wisdom was worth nothing against Shmuel’s wisdom, he asked him something he did not know how to answer.
gershom:a13.1: [Editor’s note in the printed text: Our Rabbeinu’s text had “The Sages taught: nostrils that were pierced” after the mishna of the external gums, and therefore he first explains “One does not examine from the double teeth.”] One does not examine from the double teeth inward: these are the large teeth standing at the end of the jaws, where a blemish is not seen even if they were extracted, whether through eating or through bleating. They are called mat’imot [twinned] because each has two roots. And not even the double teeth themselves: if they were extracted, it is not an exposed blemish.
gershom:a14.1: At the end of the nose, this is a blemish, for there it is seen; on the inside, in the depth of the nose, it is not a blemish, for it is not seen.
gershom:a15.1: Tura bara deshiftei: the outer skin.
gershom:a16.1: What is it saying: Rabbi Ḥananya: “One does not pay attention,” etc.
gershom:a17.1: It is disqualified: from being offered.
gershom:a18.1: Is a lack of a limb on the inside a blemish? For example, if it lacks a kidney or the spleen through cutting or through a drug.
gershom:a19.1: “Lameness or blindness” is written: something exposed and not concealed. And so too “blind or broken” are exposed. To be slaughtered or to be redeemed we have no question, for we act only on an exposed blemish.
gershom:a20.1: Just as a blemish is on the outside: as it is written, “blind or broken”; that is a blemish, and it is on the outside.
gershom:a21.1: And not one with one kidney: that was created with one.
gershom:a22.1: They assumed that everyone agrees there is no creature with one: it is not its way to be created with one. [And this] that excludes “and not one with one kidney” is where it had two and one was removed.
gershom:a23.1: He holds that a lack on the inside is called a lack. Rav Ḥiyya said, etc. And it is not difficult: what it teaches, “and not one with one kidney,” is where it was created with two and lacked one.
gershom:a24.1: Just as three were from the outset, for so it was created, so too one from the outset, for so it was created, with one. So how can you say that the teaching “and not one with one kidney” is where it was created with two and lacked one?
gershom:a25.1: If it lacked before slaughter, it is forbidden; after slaughter, it is permitted.
rashi:b1.1: One who slits the ear of the bull: the anointed priest, after slaughter.
rashi:b1.2: That already was: at the time the blood was collected, it was whole.
tosafot:b1.1: But doesn’t Rabbi Zeira say that Rav says, one who slits: In the second chapter of Zevachim (25b) the reading is: “as it is taught [in a baraita]: one who slits.”
rashi:b4.1: Interpret it as “in its year”: what it teaches, that all its stages must be [so], refers to “in its year.” But unblemished we require only at slaughter and collection.
rashi:b4.2: So too it is reasonable: that one that became lacking after collection is fit.
rashi:b4.3: An olive-bulk of flesh: so there is enough for a person to eat.
rashi:b4.4: Or an olive-bulk of fat: so there is enough for the altar to consume.
rashi:b4.5: He sprinkles the blood: but if nothing remained, he does not sprinkle, as it is written: “And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood” (Deuteronomy 12:27): if there is no flesh, there is no blood. In any case it teaches that if an olive-bulk remained he sprinkles; and you have no greater lack than this, for all of it is lacking, and yet it teaches that he sprinkles. Evidently, what it teaches, “all its stages,” refers to “in its year.”
rashi:b5.1: Hours disqualify: it comes to teach us that if this lamb was born last year on the fourteenth of Nisan at the eighth hour of the day, he must take care now to slaughter it before the ninth hour, for the ninth hour disqualifies it, and it is as if it entered its second year.
rashi:b6.1: Let us say: this dilemma of Rav Aḥadvoi is a dispute of tanna’im.
rashi:b7.1: In the testicles and not in the penis: said in astonishment. That is to say, if they were in the penis, would it not be a blemish? It certainly is more of a blemish, for the penis is more exposed than the testicles.
rashi:b7.2: Kattut [crushed]: they were crushed with stones until it dissolved.
rashi:b7.3: Nattuk [torn]: completely, by hand, but they still hang in the sac.
rashi:b7.4: Karut [cut]: with a knife, and they still hang in the sac and are slightly attached, for karut is less than nattuk, as we said in the previous chapter (Bekhorot 33b): “to include one who tears after one who cuts.” Rabbi Yosei’s reason is explained below.
rashi:b7.5: All of them on the penis: not in the testicles.
rashi:b7.6: Rabbi Yehuda holds that a lack on the inside is called a lack.
tosafot:b7.1: All of them on the penis and not in the testicles: However, the end of the verse, “nor shall you do this in your land” [Leviticus 22:24], applies even to the testicles, in any way that one castrates, for we forbid it even by [the word here is unclear in the printed text], in chapter Shemoneh Sheratzim (Shabbat 110b). It is only regarding a blemish that it does not count as an exposed blemish, as the reason is explained shortly.
rashi:b10.1: Rather, here they disagree about exposed blemishes: for everyone holds that a lack on the inside is called a lack. The one who disqualifies in the testicles does so not because of a lack but because of a blemish.
rashi:b10.2: For they hang: they hang down and knock about in the sac and are seen from outside, as they are not fastened above.
rashi:b10.3: Sometimes they shrink: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), even when they are healthy.
rashi:b11.1: For they are not there: and it is a lack.
rashi:b12.1: Mishna. Hazoven: this is the sheath in which the sac is hidden.
rashi:b12.2: And the genitalia of a female among consecrated animals: among the other consecrated animals that may be female, for among firstborns there is no female; and in peace offerings, which may be female, if the genitalia were damaged it is a blemish.
rashi:b12.3: From the joint: if it was damaged between the joints it heals, if the whole tail was not cut off but it was only slightly damaged.
rashi:b12.4: Or the end of the tail mefatzel the bone: the end that hangs down, the skin and flesh were peeled and the bone remained exposed. It no longer heals, since it is at the end of the tail. Mefatzel is as in “and he peeled [vayefatzel]” (Genesis 30[:37]).
tosafot:b12.1: Or the end of the tail mefatzel the bone: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that the skin and flesh were peeled and the bone remained exposed, as in “and he peeled.” This is difficult, for in the language of the mishna and the Talmud it should have said “and was peeled.” It seems one should explain that it splits the bone in two, like the horns that are mefutzalot (Chullin 59b), split this way and that. And so the Tosefta (chapter 4) teaches: “or the end of the tail is split into two bones.” [The mishna as printed on the daf does go on to say “the skin and the flesh were removed.”]
rashi:b13.1: Gemara. Damaged: the zoven, it is a blemish; it does not become healthy again.
rashi:b13.2: And not removed: for if it was removed it is not a blemish, as it returns to its strength.
rashi:b13.3: The sac: if it was damaged it is a blemish; but the male organ, the organ itself, that was damaged is not a blemish, for it heals.
rashi:b13.4: That a wolf took: the whole zoven.
rashi:b14.1: The fingerbreadth they spoke of, etc.: and we do not know now where it stands, and that is why he asks, for what halakha did they say it.
rashi:b14.2: One of four in a handbreadth: because the fingers are not equal, as we say in Menachot, chapter HaTekhelet (41b): a Torah handbreadth is four by the thumb, six by the little finger, five (and a third by the index finger). And it says here that wherever the Sages mentioned a fingerbreadth, we require one of four in the handbreadth of any person, which is the thumb.
rashi:b14.3: For what halakha: did they mention a fingerbreadth?
rashi:b14.4: How many threads: they mentioned this with regard to tzitzit.
tosafot:b14.1: In brief: One must examine whether Beit Shammai’s “four” means four in all, or four for the white and four for the tekhelet; and also whether it speaks of before the threads are doubled over, since once doubled they would be sixteen. On that reading, the eight threads we make now are all for the white, since we rule like Beit Shammai in chapter HaTekhelet (Menachot 41b), and if one of them is cut it is unfit; and although we approve a tekhelet agradom [the winding thread] that stands for white, all of these are for white. The Sifrei on Ki Tetzei implies four threads of each kind: “How many threads are the gedilim made of? Not fewer than three, as Beit Hillel says; Beit Shammai say: four threads of tekhelet and four of white, of four fingerbreadths; and the halakha follows Beit Shammai.” But from HaTekhelet, where Rav Yirmeya of Difti put in eight, which are sixteen, while Mar son of Ravina did as we do, it seems most followed Mar son of Ravina. Perhaps he explained Beit Shammai’s “four for the white and four for the tekhelet” as after doubling, that is, two of each kind before doubling; and then what we do now is half for white and half for tekhelet. But Beit Hillel’s three must be before doubling, since three cannot result after doubling, and so it is not then parallel to Beit Shammai’s four. Open on Sefaria for the full text.
rashi:b15.1: Meshuleshet [hanging]: hanging below the corner of the garment, for one does not place it at the very edge of the garment but raises it three fingerbreadths into the garment.
rashi:b15.2: One of four: three thumbs, each one of four in a handbreadth. Another version: meshuleshet: how much of it should be braided, apart from the anaf [the loose strands] that is not braided.
tosafot:b15.1: How much: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: hanging below the corner of the garment, for one does not place it at the very edge of the garment but raises it three fingerbreadths into the garment for Beit Hillel and four for Beit Shammai. This is difficult for his explanation, for regarding the distance from the corner we resolve [in Menachot] “the full length of a thumb joint,” and “within three fingerbreadths” is mentioned there only to exclude more than three. It seems [right to explain] as the other version the Kuntres gave: how much should be meshuleshet, that is, how much of it should be braided apart from the anaf that is not braided, and Beit Shammai say four fingerbreadths. Then the beauty of tzitzit, a third braid and two thirds anaf, is a braid of four fingerbreadths and an anaf of eight, twelve fingerbreadths in all. And so it is implied by “four of white, of four fingerbreadths.” In chapter HaTekhelet (Menachot 41b) the Kuntres explained meshuleshet as hanging in the anaf apart from the braid, four fingerbreadths; and by his explanation the beauty of tzitzit is two fingerbreadths of braid and four of anaf.
rashi:b16.1: Two cubits: two rods a cubit long.
gershom:b1.1: One who slits the ear of the bull: after slaughter, before collection.
gershom:b2.1: And sprinkling: of the lintel and the two doorposts. [Editor’s note in the printed text: According to the reading here, “and sprinkling,” our Rabbeinu is forced to explain that it speaks of the Passover in Egypt, which that verse addresses, for in the Passover of later generations we find only tossing or pouring; but in Zevachim (25a) the reading is “tossing,” and one can well say it refers to the Passover of later generations.] Interpret it as “in its year”: that is, for all its stages we require it to be in its first year, but unblemished we require only until the time of collection.
gershom:b3.1: So too it is reasonable: that we do not require it to be unblemished at the time of tossing.
gershom:b4.1: This is to say that hours disqualify in consecrated animals: that is, if at the time of slaughter it was within its year, counted from moment to moment, and between its slaughter and its tossing an hour or two passed into the next year, it is unfit.
gershom:b5.1: Rabbi Yehuda says, in the testicles and not on the penis? But on the penis it is more visible! Say: all of them also in the testicles.
gershom:b6.1: For one Sage holds: Rabbi Yehuda, who says in the testicles, holds that a lack on the inside is called a lack; and Rabbi Eliezer [ben Ya’akov] holds it is not called a lack.
gershom:b7.1: And can you understand it so, that they disagree about this? What does Rabbi Yosei hold, etc.
gershom:b8.1: Rather, here they disagree about an exposed blemish. Rabbi Yehuda holds that bruised and crushed, even in the testicles, is an exposed blemish, for they shrink afterward.
gershom:b9.1: And torn and cut: in the testicles too it is an exposed blemish, for the testicles hang lower in the sac than at first.
gershom:b10.1: And Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov holds: these, in the testicles, are not an exposed blemish, for from the outset, when it is unblemished, sometimes the sac shrinks, as the testicles go up into the belly and the sac shrinks, and sometimes they descend and hang and the sac is long. Therefore in the testicles they are not exposed blemishes, only on the penis.
gershom:b11.1: And Rabbi Yosei holds that bruised and crushed are exposed blemishes even in the testicles, for they are not there, since they dissolved.
gershom:b12.1: And torn and cut: in the testicles they are not exposed blemishes, for the testicles are there, and from the outset too they sometimes hang; but on the penis it is an exposed blemish. And how can there be “cut” in the testicles? For example, he tore the sac a little and cut the testicles, then sewed the sac up again, and the testicles remained cut within the sac.
gershom:b13.1: The zoven was damaged: that is the sac in which the organ lies.
gershom:b14.1: And the genitalia of a female among consecrated animals that was damaged around the opening. It mentions a female among consecrated animals because there is no female among firstborns.
gershom:b15.1: From the bone it is a blemish, for it does not become healthy again; but not from the joint between bone and bone, for it heals again.
gershom:b16.1: Mefatzel the bone: it is a blemish, for it does not become healthy again.
gershom:b17.1: And so too a full fingerbreadth between joint and joint is a blemish.
gershom:b18.1: The zoven was damaged, it is a blemish; and not removed, for it grows back. And so too the sac, which is the zoven, if damaged is a blemish, for it is exposed; and not if the male organ itself was damaged, for it is concealed and heals.
gershom:b19.1: That a wolf took the zoven, and afterward it returned to its strength, as it had been.
gershom:b20.1: One of four in a handbreadth of any person: as they say, four by the thumb.
gershom:b21.1: And how much should be meshuleshet: that is, how long the braided part should be.
